title: First Contact
summary: Learn your bearings in a Bash workspace.
description: A terminal is a text interface for asking the operating system to do work. Bash reads commands; it is not the operating system itself. Explore the current directory, identify the lab user, inspect the supplied files, then write the observed facts to `mission-report.txt`.
learning_objectives: Create a report with the observed facts

workspace_seed.starter.txt: Start with pwd, whoami, and ls -la.

offline_hints.title: Think about the concept
offline_hints.content: Start by asking the shell where you are and which user it is running as.

offline_hints.title: Investigate this area
offline_hints.content: Use `pwd`, `whoami`, and `ls -la`. Put the results into a small text report in `/workspace`.

offline_hints.title: Guided route
offline_hints.content: Create `/workspace/mission-report.txt` with separate lines `location=/workspace`, `user=redpanda`, and `files=field-notes.txt,starter.txt` (the exact file names, sorted alphabetically). Verify it with `cat`.

completion_explanation: The report is checked from the actual workspace file, not from a button click. `pwd` reports a path, `whoami` reports the effective user, and `ls` inventories directory entries. This is the foundation of nearly every terminal investigation.

network_requirements.description: No network interface is required for this mission.
